questions.question: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 36 ÷ 2 × 12 + 3 - 6 = 24
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

36 ÷ 2 × 12 + 3 - 6 = 24
questions.solution:
1) + and ×

Given equation: 36 ÷ 2 × 12 + 3 - 6 = 24

After interchanging ‘+ and ×’, we get:

L.H.S = 36 ÷ 2 + 12 × 3 - 6

= 18 + 36 - 6

= 54 - 6

= 48 ≠ R.H.S

2) ÷ and ×

Given equation: 36 ÷ 2 × 12 + 3 - 6 = 24

After interchanging ‘÷ and ×’, we get:

L.H.S = 36 × 2 ÷ 12 + 3 - 6

= 6 + 3 - 6

= 3 ≠ R.H.S

3) - and ÷

Given equation: 36 ÷ 2 × 12 + 3 - 6 = 24

After interchanging ‘- and ÷’, we get:

L.H.S = 36 - 2 × 12 + 3 ÷ 6

= 36 - 24 + 0.5

= 12.5 ≠ R.H.S

4) × and -

Given equation: 36 ÷ 2 × 12 + 3 - 6 = 24

After interchanging ‘× and -’, we get:

L.H.S = 36 ÷ 2 - 12 + 3 × 6

= 18 - 12 + 18

= 36 - 12

= 24 = R.H.S

Hence, ‘× and -‘ is the correct answer.

questions.question: In an exam of 80 questions, a correct answer gives 1 marks but a wrong answer deducts 1 marks, and if a question in not attempted there is no deduction in marks. If a student attempted only 80% of the question and got 32 marks, then how many questions did he answer correctly?
questions.questionHtml: In an exam of 80 questions, a correct answer gives 1 marks but a wrong answer deducts 1 marks, and if a question in not attempted there is no deduction in marks. If a student attempted only 80% of the question and got 32 marks, then how many questions did he answer correctly?
questions.solution:
Let us consider that the student answered ‘a’ answers correctly.

Now, the student attempted only 80% of the questions (given)

80% of 80 = 64

So, number of incorrect questions = (64 - a)

Also, the student scored 32 marks (given)

So, according to question:

a - (64 - a) = 32

→ a - 64 + a = 32

→ 2a = 96

→ a = 48

Hence, the student answered 48 questions correctly.

questions.question: If \(\frac{{\sec \theta \; - \;\tan \theta }}{{\sec \theta \; + \;\tan \theta }}\; = \;\frac{3}{5},\) then the value of \(\frac{{cosec\theta \; + \;\cot \theta }}{{cosec\;\theta \; - {\rm{\;cot}}\theta }}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If \(\frac{{\sec \theta \; - \;\tan \theta }}{{\sec \theta \; + \;\tan \theta }}\; = \;\frac{3}{5},\) then the value of \(\frac{{cosec\theta \; + \;\cot \theta }}{{cosec\;\theta \; - {\rm{\;cot}}\theta }}\) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Apply Componendo and Dividendo on the given equation: (sec θ − tan θ) / (sec θ + tan θ) = 3/5.

⇒ (sec θ) / (−tan θ) = (5 + 3) / (3 − 5) = 8 / −2 = −4 ⇒ sec θ / tan θ = 4 ⇒ 1/sin θ = 4 ⇒ sin θ = 1/4.

Then cosec θ = 4 and cot θ = √(cosec2θ − 1) = √15.

Expression = (4 + √15) / (4 − √15) = (4 + √15)2 / (16 − 15) = 16 + 15 + 8√15 = 31 + 8√15.

∴ The correct answer is 31 + 8√15.

Alternate Method

Given: (sec θ − tan θ) / (sec θ + tan θ) = 3/5

Formula: (a/b) = (c/d) ⇒ (a+b)/(a-b) = (c+d)/(c-d)

⇒ By cross multiplication: 5(sec θ − tan θ) = 3(sec θ + tan θ)

⇒ 5 sec θ − 5 tan θ = 3 sec θ + 3 tan θ

⇒ 2 sec θ = 8 tan θ ⇒ sec θ / tan θ = 4

⇒ (1/cos θ) / (sin θ/cos θ) = 4 ⇒ 1/sin θ = 4 ⇒ cosec θ = 4

⇒ sin θ = 1/4, so cos θ = √(1 − (1/4)2) = √15 / 4

⇒ cot θ = cos θ / sin θ = (√15 / 4) / (1/4) = √15

⇒ Required value = (4 + √15) / (4 − √15)

⇒ Rationalizing: [(4 + √15) × (4 + √15)] / [(4 − √15) × (4 + √15)]

⇒ (16 + 15 + 8√15) / (16 − 15) = 31 + 8√15

∴ The correct answer is 31 + 8√15.

Additional Information

Componendo and Dividendo

If a/b = c/d, then (a+b)/(a-b) = (c+d)/(c-d). This is useful for simplifying ratios involving trigonometric functions.

Trigonometric Identities

sec2θ − tan2θ = 1 and cosec2θ − cot2θ = 1. These identities are fundamental for converting between functions.

Rationalization

To remove radicals from the denominator, multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate (a + √b → a − √b).

Dividing by x

⇒ x6 + 1/x6 + 3 × 7 = 343

⇒ x6 + 1/x6 = 343 – 21

⇒ x6 + 1/x6 = 322

questions.question: If 2sinθ + 15cos 2 θ = 7, 0° < θ < 90°, then tanθ + cosθ + secθ = ?
questions.questionHtml: If 2sinθ + 15cos<sup>2</sup>θ = 7, 0° < θ < 90°, then tanθ + cosθ + secθ = ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Test standard values for θ: If sinθ = 1/3, then cos2θ = 1 − 1/9 = 8/9.

Substitute in equation: 2(1/3) + 15(8/9) = 2/3 + 40/3 = 42/3 = 14 (Too high).

Test sinθ = 3/5 (from 3-4-5 triplet): 2(3/5) + 15(16/25) = 6/5 + 48/5 = 54/5 = 10.8 (Too high).

Test sinθ = 1/5: 2(1/5) + 15(24/25) = 2/5 + 72/5 = 74/5 = 14.8 (Too high).

Solving the quadratic 15sin2θ − 2sinθ − 8 = 0 gives sinθ = 4/5.

For sinθ = 4/5, tanθ = 4/3, cosθ = 3/5, secθ = 5/3 → 4/3 + 3/5 + 5/3 = 3 + 3/5 = 3(3/5).

∴ The correct answer is 3(3)/(5).

Alternate Method

Given: 2sinθ + 15cos2θ = 7

Formula Used: cos2θ = 1 − sin2θ

⇒ 2sinθ + 15(1 − sin2θ) = 7

⇒ 2sinθ + 15 − 15sin2θ = 7

⇒ 15sin2θ − 2sinθ − 8 = 0

⇒ 15sin2θ − 12sinθ + 10sinθ − 8 = 0

⇒ 3sinθ(5sinθ − 4) + 2(5sinθ − 4) = 0

⇒ (3sinθ + 2)(5sinθ − 4) = 0

⇒ sinθ = 4/5 (since 0° < θ < 90°)

⇒ tanθ = 4/3, cosθ = 3/5, secθ = 5/3

⇒ tanθ + cosθ + secθ = 4/3 + 3/5 + 5/3 = 9/3 + 3/5 = 3 + 3/5 = 18/5 = 3(3/5)

∴ The correct answer is 3(3)/(5).

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include sin2θ + cos2θ = 1, 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ, and 1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common triplets like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17) help in identifying side ratios quickly when one trigonometric ratio is known.

Quadratic Roots in Trig

When solving asin2θ + bsinθ + c = 0, always check the range (e.g., −1 to 1 for sine) and the given quadrant.

questions.questionHtml: A can complete a certain piece of work in 40 days. B is 25% more efficient than A and C is 28% more efficient than B. They work together for 5 days. The remaining work will be complete by B alone, in:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Efficiency ratio A : B : C = 100 : 125 : (125 × 1.28) = 100 : 125 : 160 = 20 : 25 : 32.

Total Work = Efficiency of A × Days = 20 × 40 = 800 units.

5 days work of (A+B+C) = 5 × (20 + 25 + 32) = 5 × 77 = 385 units.

Remaining work = 800 − 385 = 415 units.

Time taken by B alone = 415 ÷ 25 = 16.6 days = 16(3/5) days.

∴ The correct answer is 16(3/5) days.

Alternate Method

Given: A completes work in 40 days. Efficiency of B is 25% more than A. Efficiency of C is 28% more than B.

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A 40 800 20
B 32 25
C 25 32

⇒ Efficiency of A = 20 (assumed to make B = 25 and C = 32)

⇒ Total Work = 40 × 20 = 800 units

⇒ Combined Efficiency (A+B+C) = 20 + 25 + 32 = 77 units/day

⇒ Work done in 5 days = 77 × 5 = 385 units

⇒ Remaining Work = 800 − 385 = 415 units

⇒ Time taken by B = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time = 415 ÷ 25 = 83 ÷ 5 = 16(3/5) days

∴ The correct answer is 16(3/5) days.

Additional Information

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken. If A is x% more efficient than B, Efficiency Ratio A:B = (100+x):100.

Total Work Formula

Total Work = Efficiency × Time. This remains constant for a specific piece of work regardless of the number of people working.

Work Done by Group

questions.question: A dealer marks an article 40% above the cost price and sells it to a customer, allowing two successive discounts of 20% and 25% on the marked price. If he suffers a loss of Rs. 140, then the cost price (in Rs) of the article is:
questions.questionHtml: A dealer marks an article 40% above the cost price and sells it to a customer, allowing two successive discounts of 20% and 25% on the marked price. If he suffers a loss of Rs. 140, then the cost price (in Rs) of the article is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let Cost Price (CP) be 100.

Marked Price (MP) = 100 × 1.40 = 140.

Successive discounts of 20% and 25% result in a net multiplier of 0.80 × 0.75 = 0.6.

Selling Price (SP) = 140 × 0.6 = 84.

Loss = CP − SP = 100 − 84 = 16 units. Given 16 units = Rs. 140.

CP = (140 ÷ 16) × 100 = 8.75 × 100 = Rs. 875.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 875.

Alternate Method

Given: Markup = 40%, Discounts = 20% and 25%, Total Loss = Rs. 140.

Formulas: MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | Net Discount% = a + b − (ab ÷ 100) | SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100

⇒ Effective Discount = 20 + 25 − (20 × 25 ÷ 100) = 45 − 5 = 40%.

⇒ Let Cost Price be x. Then Marked Price = 1.4x.

⇒ Selling Price = 1.4x × (1 − 0.40) = 1.4x × 0.6 = 0.84x.

⇒ Loss = CP − SP ⇒ 140 = x − 0.84x.

⇒ 140 = 0.16x ⇒ x = 140 ÷ 0.16 = 875.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 875.

Additional Information

Marked Price & Discount

Marked Price is the price listed on the product. Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price to arrive at the Selling Price.

Successive Discounts

When two discounts d1 and d2 are given, the equivalent single discount is [d1 + d2 − (d1 × d2 ÷ 100)]%.

questions.solution:
GIven:

(a + b – c)3 + (a – b + c)3 – 8a3

Concept used:

Trial and error

Calculation:

Let us use the trial and error method to obtain the solution.

Let a = b = c = 1

Then,

(a + b – c)3 + (a – b + c)3 – 8a3 = 1 + 1 – 8 = (-6)

Now, lets check option (1):

3a(a + b – c)(a – b + c) = 3 × (1) × (1) ≠ (-6)

Now, lets check option (2):

6a(a + b – c) (a – b + c) = 6 × (1) × (1) ≠ (-6)

Checking option 3rd.

6a(a – b + c) (c – a – b) = 6 × 1 × (-1) = (-6)

Hence, option 3 is right.

∴ The solution of the question is 6a(a – b + c) (c – a – b). 

Alternate Method(a + b - c)3 + (a - b + c)3 - 8a3

⇒ (a + b - c)3 + (a - b + c)3 - (2a)3

Let (a + b - c) = x, (a - b + c) = y, -2a = z

x + y + z = a + b - c + a - b + c - 2a

x + y + z = 0

We know that,

If, x + y + z = 0, then x3 + y3 + z3 = 3xyz

(a + b - c)3 + (a - b + c)3 + (-2a)3 = 3(a + b - c) (a - b + c) (-2a)

⇒ -6a (a + b - c) (a - b + c)

⇒ 6a(-a - b + c)(a - b + c)

⇒ 6a (a - b + c) (c - a - b)

questions.question: Anu fixes the selling price of an article at 25% above its cost of production. If the cost of production goes up by 20% and she raises the selling price by 10% then her percentage profit is (correct to one decimal place):
questions.questionHtml: Anu fixes the selling price of an article at 25% above its cost of production. If the cost of production goes up by 20% and she raises the selling price by 10% then her percentage profit is (correct to one decimal place):
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let initial cost price be 100.

Initial Selling Price = 100 × 1.25 = 125.

New Cost Price = 100 × 1.20 = 120.

New Selling Price = 125 × 1.10 = 137.5.

New Profit = 137.5 − 120 = 17.5.

Profit% = (17.5 ÷ 120) × 100 ≈ 14.6%.

∴ The correct answer is 14.6%.

Alternate Method

Given: Initial markup = 25%, CP increase = 20%, SP increase = 10%.

Formulas: Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Let Cost Price (CP1) = 100.

⇒ Selling Price (SP1) = 100 + 25% of 100 = 125.

⇒ New Cost Price (CP2) = 100 + 20% of 100 = 120.

⇒ New Selling Price (SP2) = 125 + 10% of 125 = 125 + 12.5 = 137.5.

⇒ Profit = 137.5 − 120 = 17.5.

⇒ Profit Percentage = (17.5 ÷ 120) × 100 = 1750 ÷ 120 = 14.583%.

⇒ Rounding to one decimal place, we get 14.6%.

∴ The correct answer is 14.6%.

Additional Information

Base Value for Profit

Profit is always calculated on the actual cost price unless specified otherwise. Formula: Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Markup and Selling Price

Marked Price is the price at which SP is fixed initially before any subsequent changes or discounts.

questions.question: In ΔABC, AB = AC and AL is perpendicular to BC at L. In ΔDEF, DE = DF and DM is perpendicular to EF at M. If (area of ΔABC) : (are of ΔDEF) = 9 : 25 and ∠BAC = ∠EDF, then \(\frac{{DM\; + \;AL}}{{DM - AL}}\) is equal to: Given that both the triangles are similar.

questions.solution:
Formula Used:

When two Δ are similar,

Area of Δ 1/Area of Δ 2 = (side of Δ 1)2/(side of Δ 2)2 

Calculation:

(area of ΔABC) : (are of ΔDEF) = (AL)2 : (DM)2

(AL)2 : (DM)2 = 9 : 25

AL/DM = 3/5

Let AL = 3 and DM = 5

∴ (DM + AL)/(DM – AL) = (5 + 3)/(5 – 3) = 8/2 = 4.

questions.question: A race track is in the shape of a ring whose inner and outer circumferences are 440 m and 506 m, respectively. What is the cost of levelling the track at Rs 6/m 2 ?(take π = 22/7)
questions.questionHtml: A race track is in the shape of a ring whose inner and outer circumferences are 440 m and 506 m, respectively. What is the cost of levelling the track at Rs 6/m<sup>2</sup>?(take π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Let internal and external radius of the track be r m and R m respectively.

Internal circumference of the track = 2πr

2 πr = 440

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r = 440

⇒ r = 70 m

External circumference of the track = 2πR

2 πR = 506

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × R = 506

⇒ R = 506 × (7/44)

⇒ R = 80.5 m

Area of track = π (R2 – r2) = (22/7) × (80.52 – 702) = 22/7 × 150.5 × 10.5 = 4966.5 m2

Cost of levelling 1 m2 = Rs. 6

∴ Cost of levelling 4966.5 m2 = 4966.5 × 6 = Rs. 29,799

questions.solution:
• We make changes in tenses of reported speech only when the reporting verb is in the past tense.
  • When the reported speech is an interrogative sentence we follow these steps-
    • Reporting verb 'said' is changed into 'asked'.
    • Change the sentence, given in the reported speech, from interrogative to assertive.
    • Tense of reported speech is changed accordingly. ( in above sentence- 'are' changes into 'was')

By following these steps we get the final sentence - " He asked me what I was doing."
